speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. I see you have a painful, ulcerative skin lesion on your leg; can you tell me exactly how long it has been there and how it started?

speaker: Patient
text: 54-year-old woman. The patient reports a skin lesion on her right leg that has been present for 1 month. The lesion began as a small red spot and has increased in size. She recalls an ant bite at the site before the lesion developed. She has a history of anterior uveitis treated with corticosteroids 8 months ago, as well as Crohn's disease, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and hypertension.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Pyoderma Gangrenosum.

Based on your history of Crohn's disease, diabetes, and the rapid development of a painful ulcer following a minor trauma (the "ant bite"), the clinical presentation is highly suggestive of Pyoderma Gangrenosum rather than an infectious etiology. Given your immunocompromised state, I need to confirm this before we proceed with any debridement, which could worsen the wound.

REQUEST TEST: CBC with differential, ESR, CRP, and wound culture.
REQUEST IMAGES: High-resolution photo of the lesion edges and base.
